## Structure and components

- [statement] Attempting to run models larger than 16GB across a Thunderbolt eGPU requires layer-by-layer weight streaming that collapses token generation throughput to sub-1 token per second. ## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Discrete eGPU GDDR7 achieves ~1000 GB/s memory bandwidth, delivering over 2x the memory-bound token generation throughput of Apple Silicon unified memory for models that fit within its 16GB VRAM limit. (high confidence) — https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad · keywords: MLX Unified Memory vs eGPU GDDR7 Hardware Architecture · also: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/unified_memory_architecture

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Thunderbolt 5 eGPU links provide approximately 7.0 GB/s practical unidirectional bandwidth, creating a severe bottleneck if model weights are streamed from host RAM rather than fully resident in GDDR7 VRAM. (high confidence) — https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad · keywords: MLX Unified Memory vs eGPU GDDR7 Hardware Architecture · also: https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Apple Silicon Unified Memory provides a shared address space allowing CPU and Metal GPU to operate on identical memory pointers without PCIe serialization or host-device DMA copies. (high confidence) — https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx · keywords: MLX Unified Memory vs eGPU GDDR7 Hardware Architecture · also: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/unified_memory_architecture
